blocking_finding: SS5.4.2 step 2 misdescribes earmark_parser's actual AST shape for raw HTML as a 'separately-tagged node kind' -- verified against real hexdocs/README that raw/verbatim HTML is NOT a distinct tag/node kind. Every node is a uniform 4-tuple {tag, attrs, children, meta}; raw HTML is marked by meta[:verbatim] == true on a node that otherwise carries an ordinary-looking tag (e.g. {"span", [...], [...], %{verbatim: true}}). A reasonable implementer following the design as written would branch on node tag/shape, not meta[:verbatim], silently reopening a raw-HTML bypass -- the exact failure mode recurring at the design layer instead of the regex layer.
required_fix: Correct SS5.4.2 step 2 to name the real discriminator (meta[:verbatim] == true on the walked node). Re-verify step 3's href/src attribute-list claim against the same primary source, since it was checked via the same secondary-fetch method as the now-disproven step 2 claim.
non_blocking_note: SS5.4.1's 'earmark depends on earmark_parser' lineage claim is directionally true (earmark_parser's own README self-describes as extracted from earmark) but overstated against current hex.pm data -- earmark 1.4.49 lists zero deps and its GitHub repo is archived/retired. Should say 'originally extracted from' rather than 'depends on', and flag to REVIEWER that earmark itself (not earmark_parser) is retired, for due-diligence context even though this design correctly avoids taking earmark as a dependency.
